name: logan_paul_vlog
summary: An educational video editing breakdown combining talking-head commentary with multi-panel timeline demonstrations and vlog B-roll. The editing is characterized by dynamic pacing shifts, precise sound design synchronization, and analytic visual callouts.

captions.notes: Captions primarily appear on B-roll dialogue using clean white fonts with subtle dropshadows, while educational concepts use bold outlined text.

headline.notes: Utilizes bold monospace and pixel-font headers for counters and section titles like total money counters.

callouts.notes: Retro 8-bit text tags, bounding tracking boxes, and bold directional arrows highlight technical edit decisions.

transitions.notes: Frequent hidden cuts disguised within camera pans alongside snappy punch cuts and J/L cuts for audio continuity.

rules: Cut talking-head footage every 2 to 4 seconds or punch in to maintain momentum.
Use split-screen layouts to present NLE timelines synchronously with playback footage.
Pair numeric graphic animations with matching rhythmic sound effects such as clicks or cash register chimes.
Vary cutting cadence intentionally between rapid bursts and sustained hold shots to manipulate tension.
Use motion tracking boxes to isolate and emphasize narrative focal points.
Incorporate hidden whip-pan cuts across multiple takes to simulate seamless single-take sequences.
Support key takeaway points with centered, all-caps monospace lower-third banners.
Cut precisely on musical beats or impactful voiceover consonants.
Use a persistent split-screen showing talking head, output monitor, and active NLE timeline.
Cut every 1.5 to 3 seconds during dynamic breakdown sequences.
Punch in with rapid zooms on facecam to emphasize comedic or intense reactions.
Use distinct retro 8-bit text styling for technical labels and annotations.
avoid: Static talking-head shots lasting longer than 5 seconds without scale changes.
Flashy decorative transitions like wipes or page peels.
Unmotivated sound effects unrelated to the visual theme.
Overlapping captions that obscure key UI elements or faces.
Uncut real-time footage that drags narrative momentum.
Slow lingering shots without motion or visual change.
Overly glossy or cinematic 3D motion graphics.
